items.coder_A: has_eligible_candidate=true (flagged: in situ vaccination could be read as a cancer vaccine)
items.reason: No antigen product, cell therapy or vaccine is given; the adjuvants themselves are the tested antitumour treatment ("Immune adjuvants will be injected intratumorally and systemically to induce antitumor-specific immunity after radiation induced immunological tumor cell death"). R4 makes adjuvants part of an excluded therapy only when they support a cell therapy or vaccine; here they are tested in their own right (own arm, PFS/OS outcomes), which is R4's exception.

items.coder_A: experimental_combination (flagged: may not be a licensed medicine)
items.proposed: experimental_combination, subject to R5 licensing check
items.reason: MnCl2 is registered as one of the "enhanced immunal adjuvants (GM-CSF, Sapylin, MnCl2)"; under R5 a trace-element/supplement-type product is a candidate only if licensed as a medicine somewhere. The record gives no licensing information, so this must be checked and recorded in Table S2.

The experimental arm gives "combined stereotactic radiosurgery and enhanced immunal adjuvants (GM-CSF, Sapylin, MnCl2)"; regimen counts all antitumour therapy in the experimental arm, so all three agents and radiosurgery are recorded, as coder A did.

note: Two XL decisions: (1) whether an 'in situ vaccination' with adjuvants and radiosurgery, but no antigen product, is a cancer vaccine (excluded) or a pharmacological candidate regimen; proposal treats the adjuvants as candidates under R4's exception. (2) R5 licensing evidence for manganese chloride (and for Sapylin, a Streptococcus-derived preparation with no INN in the record) must be recorded in Table S2; S6 holds as long as at least one of the three (e.g. GM-CSF, a licensed cytokine) is a candidate. GM-CSF moiety not specified in the record (sargramostim vs molgramostim) for the [LOOKUP] step.
